new_statements.quote: El acento cae en la penúltima sílaba de la palabra. Sin embargo, cada dialecto del náhuatl divide algunas palabras en diferente numero de silabas. Por ejemplo: náhuatl de Guerrero ki.kóch.tia / náhuatl de Tlamacazapa ki.koch.tí.ya
new_statements.translation: Stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word. However, each dialect of Nahuatl divides some words into a different number of syllables. For example: Guerrero Nahuatl ki.KOCH.tia / Tlamacazapa Nahuatl ki.koch.TI.ya

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress falls on the penultimate syllable. Because Tlamacazapa Nahuatl syllabifies some words differently from Guerrero Nahuatl (e.g. a final -tiya where Guerrero has -tia), the surface position of stress in cognates can differ between the two, but each follows the penultimate rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. The authors add only that the two dialects syllabify some words differently, so the stressed syllable of a cognate can differ (Guerrero ki.kóch.tia vs Tlamacazapa ki.koch.tí.ya). My own observation, not the source's claim: a handful of entries in the vocabulary body carry written acute accents (Tlamacazapa kalsón 'calzón', keníon 'como', ichikólotzin, mixámana; Guerrero aík, átioj, káltzon), which may mark non-penultimate stress on those items; the source does not explain them.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('de la palabra'); the statement is made for both varieties of the comparative vocabulary jointly, with a Tlamacazapa example; citation forms (vocabulary entries).
new_statements.identity_note: The source is a joint comparative vocabulary of Guerrero Nahuatl [ngu, guer1241; the Atliaca/Tixtla-area variety per its map and coordinates] and Tlamacazapa Nahuatl [nuz, tlam1239; the Santiago barrio of Tlamacazapa, Taxco municipality, ~1,548 speakers per the 2000 census as cited there]. The stress sentence is stated once for both varieties together, with a Tlamacazapa example (ki.koch.tí.ya). SIL's catalogue tags the item with both ISO codes. The same sentence was already logged for guer1241 in this audit; it is the one first-hand statement for tlam1239.

sources.locator: Front matter, section 'El orden alfabético en náhuatl', p. ix (PDF p. 10), last paragraph
sources.note: Front matter 'El orden alfabético en náhuatl', p. ix (PDF p. 10): stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word in both varieties; the two dialects syllabify some words differently, so the stressed syllable differs, e.g. Guerrero ki.kóch.tia vs Tlamacazapa ki.koch.tí.ya. No separate phonology chapter; the grammar notes (pp. 184-218) say nothing further about accent. A few vocabulary entries carry written acute accents (e.g. Tlamacazapa kalsón, keníon, ichikólotzin, mixámana; Guerrero aík, átioj, káltzon), unexplained by the authors.
